transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-07-13, Start: 16:00 PDT, Duration: ~48 minutes. Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Rita Gomez (CTO, Valerian), Leo Park (ML Eng Lead), Sofia Duarte (Infra)

Summary: initial throughput / latency scoping for Valerian's customer-chat product. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Main constraints: 3s streaming p95 for long flows, 600ms p95 for short interactive completions, steady-state 50 RPS with bursts to 200 RPS, target concurrency ~300 active chat sessions, emphasis on token/sec during streaming. Discussion includes KV cache behavior, quantization tradeoffs, VPC networking and KMS.

Topics: scope, target SLOs, benchmark plan, security/SSO/KMS, deployment recommendation, next steps

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off — Maya from Redwood, AE. we're joined by Arjun, our SE. can folks quick intro?
[00:12] Rita Gomez: hi this is Rita, CTO at Valerian Systems. we run a SaaS customer support chatbot, mixed short replies & long form summarization.
[00:18] Leo Park: Leo here, I lead ML eng, we manage models in-house but exploring hybrid, and want to understand latency at scale.
[00:25] Sofia Duarte: Sofia, infra, networking and security owner.
[00:32] Arjun Patel: great — thanks. quick agenda: baseline current stacks, target p95s and concurrency, discuss hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, sketch benchmark plan. sound ok?
[00:40] Rita: yep. one thing up front: we need clear numbers — p95s and cost tradeoffs, and any network egress considerations for EU customers.
[00:47] Maya: understood. can you share current metrics?
[00:50] Leo: right now our in-house setup is gpt-medium-ish (internal) on k8s, we do 30 RPS steady with spikes to 150 for promos, token rates vary. p95 for quick intents is about 750 to 900 ms for 120 token completions, streaming isn't great — we chunk. for long form (2k tokens) we see 6 to 8s tail latency because of our batching.
[01:12] Arjun: okay that helps. what would be your p95 SLOs to be comfortable in production?
[01:16] Rita: target 600 ms p95 for typical chat replies (<=150 tokens), and for long generative streaming flows we want 3s p95 for the first 512 tokens and sustained token/sec after that. concurrency wise we plan for 300 active sessions, but only ~80% streaming at any given time.
[01:32] Sofia: and security/lightning note: we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, and option to keep keys in our KMS — ideally bring-your-own-key. also data residency EU for some customers.
[01:45] Arjun: makes sense, we support BYOK via customer KMS, SAML SSO, and Private deployments for VPC peering and regional residency. Dedicated offers guaranteed capacity if you need steady throughput.
[01:57] Leo: curious on what you mean by guaranteed capacity — is that reserved GPUs per tenant? and how does autoscaling work for bursts?
[02:04] Maya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pool, you get predictable throughput and a burst quota. autoscaling can be configured with buffer nodes; for spikes Redwood can route to fallback model variants or host-mode with transient capacity.
[02:17] Arjun: also note there's smart routing — policy based. you can route sensitive EU traffic to private regional endpoints, fallback to a less expensive quantized model if capacity constrained.
[02:27] Leo: quantization — do you see quality regression for our summarization tasks? we need to keep ROUGE/QA high.
[02:33] Arjun: quality depends on model and quant level. for 4-bit we often see minimal regression on classification & short completions, for long-form summarization we'd recommend 8-bit for pilot, and run evals against your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
[02:49] [02:49] Sofia: networking — what's latency overhead for VPC peering + private deployment vs hosted?
[02:53] Arjun: typically additional network hop adds ~5-20 ms depending on peering topology and egress. biggest contributors will be model compute and tokenization. we've seen Dedicated with colocated VPC add small jitter but gives predictable throughput.
[03:07] Leo: good. for benchmarking, we want token/sec numbers, p95 distribution, and concurrency behavior. what's your recommended runner?
[03:13] Arjun: we'll provide a benchmark harness (we call it the synthetic token-burst harness) — it simulates steady-state RPS and controlled bursts, supports streaming clients and chunks, and can collect per-token latencies. we'll share a template harness and a sample CSV result.
[03:26] Rita: and will you run that against Hosted or Dedicated? we want both, ideally.
[03:30] Maya: start with Hosted to get profile numbers, then Dedicated pilot for guaranteed throughput. for ultra-sensitive data/prod EU residency, we can propose Private deployment.
[03:40] Leo: our initial pilot goal: validate we can hit 50 RPS steady with 300 concurrent chats, p95 <=600ms for <=150 tokens, and 3s p95 for first 512 tokens on streaming. bursts to 200 RPS sustained for ~5 minutes. can Redwood show numbers for that?
[03:58] Arjun: yes we can run those scenarios. two clarifications: 1) for streaming p95 of 3s do you mean time to first token or time to 512 tokens? 2) for long flows, do you accept progressive first-token fast path and then sustained tokens/sec?
[04:12] Rita: time to first 512 tokens, meaning initial chunk throughput. we want to ensure user doesn't wait too long for the first chunk and the stream remains smooth.
[04:20] Arjun: understood. our streaming SLOs typically separate TTF (time to first token) and sustained tokens/sec. we can measure both and present p95 for TTF and for throughput windows.
[04:30] Sofia: can you explain KV cache behavior? we have lots of repeated prefixes for customer context; caching could save tokens and latency if supported.
[04:38] Arjun: yes — Redwood runtime supports KV cache across requests for chat sessions. prefix caching reduces compute and latency on repeated context. note: for Private deployments, cache hotness is higher as you control locality. some transcriptions show 'KV cash' in older logs but it's KV cache.
[04:52] Leo: ok, how about burst cost tradeoffs — do you charge for bursts differently?
[04:56] Maya: billing depends on Hosted usage; Dedicated has committed capacity pricing with overage for bursts. we'll include an estimated cost sensitivity matrix in the follow-up.
[05:05] Rita: security: need audit logs, retention controls, and keys never leave our control for some customers. can you do an air-gapped option?
[05:13] Maya: Private on-prem package is available for air-gapped, and Private VPC gives control plane separation and audit logs. we also have compliance add-ons for log retention.
[05:22] Arjun: for the pilot, recommended approach: 1) Redwood runs Hosted benchmark to get baseline latency and token/sec; 2) run the same harness on a Dedicated pilot (reserved pool sized to your steady-state plus burst); 3) evaluate Private if EU-residency or BYOK is required. we'll include model variants (standard vs quantized) to show quality vs perf tradeoffs.
[05:41] Leo: sounds good. what do you need from us?
[05:44] Maya: sample prompts, p95 target confirmations (you gave them), traffic pattern (steady RPS + bursts), and a security contact to receive SOC2 and KMS docs.
[05:52] Leo: I'll share prompts and traffic shape. Sofia will take SOC2 and KMS details.
[05:57] Rita: timeline — we want pilot results within two weeks of kickoff. is that realistic?
[06:02] Arjun: for Hosted baseline yes within 3-5 business days once we receive prompts. Dedicated pilot depends on capacity reservation but 7-10 business days after reserved pool is available.
[06:12] Maya: we'll try to expedite. next step I'll send the benchmark harness + security pack tomorrow.
[06:18] Sofia: one more thing — do you support per-route throttles and per-token accounting? we need per-customer cost attribution.
[06:26] Arjun: yes the Console has token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards; can export cost by API key, route, or model.
[06:34] Leo: edge case: what happens on model fallbacks mid-session? we worry about continuity when you fallback to quantized variant, not to change output semantics drastically.
[06:42] Arjun: we support textual continuity via deterministic fallback policies and we can pin versions at session start. fallback is best-effort — we'll record regression metrics and you can set automatic rollback if quality dips.
[06:54] Rita: ok — final recap please?
[06:58] Maya: recap: Redwood to share harness + security docs by 2026-07-14; customer to send prompts and traffic shapes by 2026-07-16; Redwood to run Hosted baseline within ~3 business days of receiving artifacts; schedule Dedicated pilot week of 2026-07-20. action items assigned.
[07:18] Leo: thanks everyone.
[07:20] Maya: appreciate the time. we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker turn attribution automated; minor mis-transcriptions present (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, model names slightly garbled).

References / links mentioned: "benchmark harness template" (will be shared by Redwood), "SOC2 report" (Redwood security pack), "sample CSV results" (benchmarks)

End of transcript.
